title: A finite ingress reduces squared fit error by 3.1 percent for the KIC 4078638 dip in Kepler quarter 4
abstract: We tested the onset of the known dip on KIC 4078638 at BKJD 355.5 in public Kepler release 25 quarter 4 data. A linear ingress with exponential recovery reduces the main squared fit error by 3.1 percent relative to an abrupt loss with full recovery. The fitted ingress is 3.26 hours. An extra guard near a pointing-loss flag cuts the main fit gain by about 94 percent. Of 6 overlapping real-flux controls with an abrupt loss added, 0 give a larger fit gain. Conditional residual-block draws and 36 sensitivity fits are included. These tests do not identify the event cause or establish a comet. The onset profiles, local baseline, gaps, noise assumptions, and one telescope limit the result. We report no new planet, comet, or independent observation. The package contains the exact raw input, hashes, code, all fits and controls, numerical checks, and offline instructions.
